title: Semicolons
concept: Semicolons terminate statements in XIOM. Omitting them on the last line of a block makes it a return value.
why: The semicolon is the most subtle character in XIOM — it controls whether a value is used or discarded.
syntax_ref:
statement;         // semicolon terminates statement
final_expression   // NO semicolon — becomes return value

// After if/match/block expressions, semicolon goes OUTSIDE:
let x = if c { a } else { b };  // ; belongs to the let
let x = match v { _ => r };     // ; belongs to the let
tips: Every statement ends with `;` — declarations, assignments, function calls
The LAST expression in a value-returning block has NO semicolon
If-expression branches don't get semicolons on their result values
If your function returns Int but you get a Unit error, check for stray semicolons
common_mistakes: Adding semicolon to the tail expression (type error: expected Int, got Unit)
Putting semicolons inside if-expression branches: `{ value; }` discards the value
